 Selangor Flood Losses More Than Double To RM52.9 Million In 2025
 By Business Today Editorial 
 November 17, 2026 
 Share 
 Facebook Twitter WhatsApp Linkedin 
 Flood-related losses in Selangor more than doubled to RM52.9 million in 2025, up from RM22.6 million in 2024, with infrastructure damage accounting for the largest share.
 State Youth, Sports and Entrepreneurship Committee chairman Mohd Najwan Halimi said the figures were based on the Selangor State Flood Loss Value Statistics for 2024 and 2025 compiled by the Department of Statistics Malaysia (DOSM). 
 Infrastructure damage amounted to RM26.6 million, followed by losses to residences at RM15.3 million, agriculture at RM9.6 million, vehicles at RM4 million and business premises at RM1 million.
 Despite the increase in Selangor, nationwide flood losses fell to RM636.9 million in 2025 from RM933.4 million in 2024, according to DOSM’s Special Report on the Impact of Floods in Malaysia 2025.
 All states were affected, with Terengganu recording the highest losses at RM89.2 million, followed by Kelantan at RM88.5 million and Johor at RM72.1 million.
 Speaking at the Selangor State Legislative Assembly sitting, Mohd Najwan said the state government would work to improve aid delivery, particularly for communities repeatedly affected by floods.
 He added that the issue would be discussed with the State Disaster Management Unit.
